lines.text: A heat pad warms your hands. Which part loses energy when your hands gain it?

Enthalpy change is the heat transferred at constant pressure, delta H equals H products minus H reactants. Exothermic reactions transfer energy from the reacting system to the surroundings, products have lower enthalpy and delta H is less than zero. Endothermic reactions absorb energy from the surroundings, products have higher enthalpy and delta H is greater than zero. The sign describes the reacting system, not the surroundings.
These energy differences become the vertical separations in reaction pathway diagrams.
Exothermic, energy released to surroundings, delta H is less than zero. Endothermic, energy absorbed from surroundings, delta H is greater than zero.
Why does warming of the surroundings imply a negative reaction enthalpy?

A reaction warms the surrounding solution. Which description is correct? Exothermic, positive enthalpy change. Endothermic, negative enthalpy change. Exothermic, negative enthalpy change. Endothermic, positive enthalpy change. C The solution gains energy because the reacting system loses it. Confusing those two systems reverses the sign.
A reaction can release energy overall and still need ignition. A pathway diagram separates the barrier from the overall change.

Label the vertical axis enthalpy and the horizontal axis progress of reaction. Draw reactants, a curve rising to a peak, and products. Products are below reactants for an exothermic reaction and above for an endothermic reaction. Forward activation energy E a is the vertical gap from reactants to the peak. delta H is products minus reactants, draw its arrow from reactant level to product level. Reverse activation energy is measured from products to the same peak. Do not use the peak when calculating the overall enthalpy change.
The sign learned for exothermic and endothermic reactions fixes the relative levels before you draw the barrier.
Axes, enthalpy against progress of reaction. Forward E a, peak minus reactants, delta H, products minus reactants.
Why can an endothermic reaction have a forward activation energy larger than its enthalpy change?

Which gap gives forward activation energy? Reactants to peak. Reactants to products. Products to peak. Zero enthalpy to peak. ay The forward reaction starts at the reactant level, so its barrier is measured from there, not from products or an arbitrary zero.
An enthalpy value is only useful if you know the conditions and the amount of reaction it describes.

Standard conditions in this syllabus are two hundred and ninety eight kelvin and one hundred and one kilopascals, indicated by standard. A standard state is the most stable physical form under those conditions. Enthalpy change of reaction, delta H r, refers to the stoichiometric amounts in the equation. Formation, delta H f, forms one mole of compound from its elements. Combustion, delta H c, completely burns one mole of substance in oxygen. Neutralisation, delta H neutralisation, is the enthalpy change when an aqueous acid and aqueous alkali react to form one mole of water. Standard enthalpy changes require standard conditions and standard states, standard formation specifically starts from elements in their standard states. An element in its standard state has standard formation enthalpy zero.
The definition decides which mole amount belongs in the denominator of a calorimetry calculation.

Standard conditions, two hundred and ninety eight kelvin, one hundred and one kilopascals, specify standard states. Formation, one mole of compound from elements, combustion, one mole completely burned. Neutralisation, one mole of water formed, reaction, equation as written.
Why can one mole of acid be the wrong basis for an enthalpy of neutralisation?

What fixes the mole basis for enthalpy of neutralisation? One mole of acid, regardless of its formula. One mole of water formed. One mole of each reagent initially added. One mole of the salt formed. B Neutralisation enthalpy is per mole of water formed. An acid can supply more than one acidic proton, so acid moles need not equal water moles.
If breaking bonds requires energy, how can a chemical reaction heat its surroundings?

Breaking bonds absorbs energy because bonded atoms must be separated against their attraction. Making bonds releases energy as atoms enter a lower energy bonded arrangement. Both processes contribute to a reaction. The reaction is exothermic when making product bonds releases more energy than breaking reactant bonds absorbs, it is endothermic when bond breaking requires more than bond making releases.
This energy balance gives the subtraction used in bond energy calculations.
Bond breaking absorbs energy, bond making releases energy. Compare the total energy absorbed and released to determine the reaction sign.
Why is it incorrect to say that a fuel releases heat by breaking its bonds?

Which explanation describes an exothermic reaction? Breaking bonds releases more than making bonds absorbs. Only bond formation occurs. Breaking and forming bonds both release energy. Making bonds releases more than breaking bonds absorbs. D Bond breaking always requires energy. Net release occurs because bond formation releases the larger total, not because bond breaking releases heat.
A balanced equation tells you how many bonds contribute, not just which bond types occur.

Use the balanced equation to count every bond broken and formed. Bond energies are positive energies for breaking gaseous bonds. Multiply each bond energy by its bond count, add the broken bond energies, then subtract the formed bond total, delta H r is approximately the sum of E open bracket broken close bracket minus the sum of E open bracket formed close bracket. For H two gas plus C L two gas yields two H C L gas, break one H H and one chlorine chlorine bond and form two H chlorine bonds. With energies four hundred and thirty six, two hundred and forty two and four hundred and thirty one kilojoules per mole, respectively, the estimate is four hundred and thirty six plus two hundred and forty two minus two open bracket four hundred and thirty one close bracket equals minus one hundred and eighty four kilojoules per mole for the equation as written.
Bond breaking and making explain the subtraction, average data explain why the result is an estimate.
Count bonds using the balanced equation. delta H r is approximately the sum of E open bracket broken close bracket minus the sum of E open bracket formed close bracket.
Why must the H chlorine energy be multiplied by two in this reaction?

For H two gas plus C L two gas yields two H C L gas, use H H four hundred and thirty six, chlorine chlorine two hundred and forty two, H chlorine four hundred and thirty one kilojoules per mole. Which estimate is correct? minus one hundred and eighty four kilojoules per mole plus one hundred and eighty four kilojoules per mole plus one thousand five hundred and forty kilojoules per mole plus two hundred and forty seven kilojoules per mole ay Subtract twice the H chlorine energy from the sum for H H and chlorine chlorine. Reversing the subtraction, adding both totals, or counting only one H chlorine bond gives the alternatives.
Why can a correct bond energy calculation disagree with a measured reaction enthalpy?

An exact bond dissociation enthalpy belongs to a specified bond breaking process in a specified gaseous species, such as splitting gaseous hydrogen molecules into gaseous atoms. An average bond energy is a mean, a tabulated value commonly averages a bond type over different gaseous compounds. Molecular environment affects bond energy, so the same bond type need not have the same value everywhere. Successive bond dissociations in methane also differ, the mean C H energy in methane is one quarter of its total gaseous atomisation enthalpy, not simply the first dissociation energy. Here exact means specific to a process, not free from experimental uncertainty.
Average values make bond energy calculations useful estimates rather than guaranteed experimental results.
Exact bond dissociation enthalpy, a specified gaseous bond breaking process. Average bond energies represent means, molecular environment matters.
Why is the first C H bond dissociation in methane not necessarily equal to its mean C H bond energy?

Which statement about a tabulated average C H bond energy is correct? It is exact for every C H bond. It is always the first methane bond dissociation energy. It averages values and may differ from a particular bond dissociation enthalpy. It is negative because breaking bonds releases energy. C An average need not match any particular bond breaking process, the surrounding molecular structure affects the energy required.
A thermometer measures the solution, while the question asks about the reacting chemicals. Keep their energy transfers separate.

Find the total mass of heated water or solution, using density and combined volume when appropriate. Calculate delta T equals T final minus T initial and q solution equals m c delta T in joules. Calculate initial reactant moles and compare them using the balanced equation to identify the limiting reactant. Use the amount actually reacted on the requested mole basis, for neutralisation use moles of water formed. If heat loss and the calorimeter heat capacity are negligible, q reaction equals minus q solution. Hence delta H equals minus q solution over open bracket one thousand n close bracket in kilojoules per mole. A rise in solution temperature means a negative reaction enthalpy.
Standard enthalpy definitions determine the mole basis, exothermic energy transfer determines the minus sign.

Use total heated solution mass in q equals m c delta T. Find limiting moles and the requested mole basis. delta H equals minus q over open bracket one thousand n close bracket in kilojoules per mole when q is in joules.
Why do you include excess reagent solution in the heated mass but not count excess reagent as reacted moles?

Two solutions react in an insulated cup. Which mass belongs in the heat calculation for their temperature rise? Only the limiting solute mass. The total mass of the mixed solution. Only the acid solution mass. Only the excess solute mass. B Both solutions undergo the measured temperature change. Limiting reactant moles determine the reacted amount, but do not replace the total heated mass.

Three processes are described. one. H plus aqueous plus O H minus aqueous gives H two O liquid. two. C H four gas plus two O two gas gives C O two gas plus two H two O liquid. three. N H three gas gives N H three liquid. Which statement is correct?
Neutralisation, combustion and condensation all release heat, so each has negative enthalpy change. B incorrectly calls neutralisation endothermic.

One commercially available heat pad contains iron, activated carbon and water. The heat pad is activated by air. This causes the pad to get hotter. Which statement describes the chemical reaction occurring in the heat pad when it is exposed to air?
The pad gets hotter because the reaction releases heat, iron is oxidised and loses electrons. C has the heat direction right but incorrectly says iron gains electrons.

A reaction pathway diagram for the reaction of aqueous sodium hydroxide and dilute sulfuric acid is shown. energy progress of reaction. two N ay O H plus H two S O four. N A two S O four plus two H two O y x. What is the value of the enthalpy change of neutralisation, delta H neutralisation?
The diagram's x is the enthalpy change for the equation as written. It produces two moles of water, so neutralisation enthalpy is x over two, A misses this division.
The reaction pathway for the forward reaction of a reversible reaction is shown. energy. in kilojoules per mole progress of reaction. thirty. fifty. Which statement is correct?

The reverse activation barrier is the forward barrier plus the vertical difference between reactants and products, fifty plus thirty equals eighty kilojoules moles minus one. B mistakes the enthalpy gap for the forward reaction.
Which equation represents the enthalpy change of atomisation of iodine?
Atomisation forms one mole of gaseous atoms from the element in its standard state, solid iodine. B starts with gaseous iodine and produces two moles of atoms.
Which equation represents an enthalpy change that is the average bond energy of the C H bond in methane?
Breaking the four C H bonds in methane and dividing the enthalpy by four gives their mean bond energy. C represents four times that mean, the common error.
For which reaction is the enthalpy change an enthalpy change of formation?
B forms one mole of N O from nitrogen and oxygen in their standard states. A starts from gaseous carbon instead of graphite.

When one point zero moles of ethanoic acid, C H three C O O H, in aqueous solution is neutralised by an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide, fifty five kilojoules per mole of energy is released. Which statement about this reaction is correct?
Making bonds releases energy and breaking them absorbs energy. The reaction is exothermic because bond formation releases more, C reverses these directions.

In an experiment, one point six zero grams of a fuel is burnt. forty five point zero percent of the energy released is absorbed by two hundred grams of water. The temperature of the water rises from eighteen point zero degrees Celsius to sixty six point zero degrees Celsius. What is the total energy released per gram of fuel burnt?

Water absorbs two hundred times four point one eight times forty eight equals forty thousand one hundred and twenty eight J. Divide by zero point four five zero and then by one point six zero g to obtain about fifty five thousand seven hundred J g minus one, A fails to account for the fraction absorbed.

When zero point four seven grams of a hydrocarbon is completely burnt in air, the energy released heats two hundred grams of water from twenty three point seven degrees Celsius to forty one point zero degrees Celsius. What is the amount of energy absorbed, in Joules, by the water?

For the water, q equals m c delta T uses m equals two hundred g and delta T equals forty one point zero minus twenty three point seven equals seventeen point three K. A uses the fuel mass and D uses absolute temperature instead of a temperature change.

A student mixes twenty five point zero cubic centimetres of zero point three five zero moles per cubic decimetre sodium hydroxide solution with twenty five point zero cubic centimetres of. zero point three five zero moles per cubic decimetre hydrochloric acid. The temperature increases by two point five degrees Celsius. No heat is lost to the surroundings. The final mixture has a specific heat capacity of four point two joules per cubic centimetre. per kelvin. What is the molar enthalpy change for the reaction?

The mixture absorbs fifty point zero times four point two times two point five equals five hundred and twenty five J. n equals zero point zero two five zero times zero point three five zero equals zero point zero zero eight seven five moles, hence delta H equals minus zero point five two five over zero point zero zero eight seven five equals minus sixty kilojoules moles minus one, C effectively uses the wrong mole count.

In order to determine the enthalpy of neutralisation of a strong acid and a strong alkali, twenty five point zero cubic centimetres of two point zero zero moles decimetres three sodium hydroxide is added to twenty five point zero cubic centimetres of two point zero zero moles decimetres three hydrochloric acid. The increase in temperature is twelve degrees Celsius. In a second experiment, the same method is used, but fifty point zero cubic centimetres of two point zero zero moles decimetres three sodium hydroxide is added to fifty point zero cubic centimetres of two point zero zero moles decimetres three hydrochloric acid. What is the increase in temperature in the second experiment?
Doubling both solution volumes doubles heat released and the mass warmed, so delta T remains twelve degrees Celsius. C doubles heat without doubling mass.
In an exothermic reaction, how do product enthalpy and delta H compare with those of reactants?
Exothermic means heat is released, products are lower in enthalpy, so products minus reactants is negative.

For a particular reversible reaction the backward reaction is endothermic. The activation energy of the backward reaction is one hundred and sixty kilojoules per mole. It can be assumed that the backward reaction proceeds by a mechanism that is the exact reverse of the mechanism for the forward reaction. Which statement about the activation energy of the forward reaction is correct?

The backward reaction is endothermic, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Both directions pass over the same energy barrier, so the backward activation energy equals the forward activation energy plus the size of the enthalpy change. The forward activation energy is therefore positive but less than one hundred and sixty kilojoules per mole, B. The printed option B has lost the words greater than.

five point one Enthalpy change, delta H.
In one breath.
A reaction transfers energy as bonds break and form. The enthalpy change tells you whether energy is released or absorbed overall, per amount of reaction specified by the equation.
Key ideas.

The enthalpy change is delta H equals H products minus H reactants. In an exothermic reaction, energy transfers to the surroundings, products lie lower in enthalpy, and delta H is less than zero. In an endothermic reaction, energy is taken in, products lie higher, and delta H is greater than zero. A warm heat pad signals an exothermic process. Do not assign a positive sign because the surroundings warmed, their gain is the reacting system's loss.

A reaction pathway diagram plots enthalpy vertically against progress of reaction horizontally. The curve rises to a maximum before falling to the product level. The forward activation energy, E a, is the gap from reactants to that maximum, delta H is the gap from reactants to products, with its sign. For the reverse reaction, measure activation energy from products to the same peak. For example, with reactants at twenty, products at fifty and peak at one hundred kilojoules per mole, the forward reaction has E a equals eighty kilojoules per mole, the reverse has E a equals fifty kilojoules per mole, and delta H equals plus thirty kilojoules per mole.

In the endothermic profile, products lie above reactants and delta H is greater than zero, in the exothermic profile they lie below and delta H is less than zero. Both forward activation energies run from reactants to the peak.

The standard symbol standard means measurements at two hundred and ninety eight kelvin and one hundred and one kilopascals in this syllabus. A substance's standard state is its most stable physical form under those conditions. The standard enthalpy change of reaction, delta H r standard, is for the stoichiometric amounts in the equation, with substances in standard states. The standard enthalpy change of formation, delta H f standard, forms one mole of a compound from its constituent elements in their standard states. For instance, graphite, rather than gaseous carbon atoms, is the standard form of carbon. An element in its standard state has delta H f standard equals zero by definition.

The standard enthalpy change of combustion, delta H c standard, is for one mole of a substance completely burned in oxygen. The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation, delta H neutralisation standard, is when an aqueous acid and aqueous alkali form one mole of water. If the balanced equation forms two moles of water, divide its reaction enthalpy by two to quote neutralisation enthalpy.
Method.

Bond energies, Draw or inspect the molecules and count bonds changed using the balanced equation. Breaking a bond absorbs energy, forming a bond releases it. Use delta H r is approximately the sum of E open bracket bonds broken close bracket minus the sum of E open bracket bonds formed close bracket. A tabulated average bond energy is a mean over bonds of the same type in different gaseous molecules. An exact bond dissociation enthalpy refers to a specified bond breaking process in a specified gaseous species. The estimate may differ from an experimental enthalpy because the molecular environments differ.

Calorimetry, Find the mass m of water or solution being heated, its temperature change delta T, and its specific heat capacity c. Calculate q equals m c delta T in joules. Find the moles n of the reactant specified by the question, then delta H equals minus q over n, converting joules to kilojoules when reporting kilojoules per mole. A temperature rise gives a negative reaction enthalpy.
Worked example.

In H two gas plus C L two gas yields two H C L gas, bond energies are H H four hundred and thirty six, chlorine chlorine two hundred and forty two and H chlorine four hundred and thirty one kilojoules per mole. Broken bonds require four hundred and thirty six plus two hundred and forty two equals six hundred and seventy eight kilojoules per mole. Two H chlorine bonds form and release two open bracket four hundred and thirty one close bracket equals eight hundred and sixty two kilojoules per mole. delta H r is approximately six hundred and seventy eight minus eight hundred and sixty two equals minus one hundred and eighty four kilojoules per mole. The negative sign is consistent with the larger energy release on bond formation.

Traps.
Trap, Label the peak to product gap as forward activation energy. Why it's wrong, The forward reaction starts at reactants. Instead, Measure its barrier from the reactant level.
Trap, Reverse the bond energy subtraction. Why it's wrong, Breaking absorbs and forming releases. Instead, Subtract the formed bond total from the broken bond total.

Trap, Put the fuel mass into q equals m c delta T. Why it's wrong, The measured temperature rise is for the water or solution. Instead, Use that heated mass, then divide by moles of fuel or other specified reactant.
Exam technique.

For define, include the one mole basis, standard states, and standard conditions where relevant. For calculate, show the counted bonds or the q substitution, use the correct mole denominator, state the sign, and give units. A temperature difference has the same numerical value in kelvin and degrees Celsius, do not add two hundred and seventy three to a temperature rise.
